summary: 这篇书评通过托马斯·杨在光学、视觉和古文字破译等领域的贡献，考察“通才”意味着什么。传记展现了他惊人的研究广度，同时也暴露出私人生活材料相对稀少的难题。
logic: 梳理科学与古文字成就
评价传记可以还原的生活侧面

paragraphs.brief: Thomas Young(1773-1829年)为伟大的英国百科全书、百科全书、英国百科百科全刊撰写了63篇文章，其中包括46个传记(主要是关于科学家和古典学者的)和关于 " 布里奇 " (一张纸牌游戏)、" 埃及 "、" 语言 " 和 " 潮流 " 的实质性文章。
sentences: Thomas Young (1773–1829) contributed 63 articles to the great British encyclopaedia, Encyclopaedia Britannica, including 46 biographical entries (mostly on scientists and classical scholars) and substantial essays on ‘Bridge’ (a card game), ‘Egypt’, ‘Languages’ and ‘Tides’.
Thomas Young(1773-1829年)为伟大的英国百科全书、百科全书、英国百科百科全刊撰写了63篇文章，其中包括46个传记(主要是关于科学家和古典学者的)和关于 " 布里奇 " (一张纸牌游戏)、" 埃及 "、" 语言 " 和 " 潮流 " 的实质性文章。
Was someone who could write authoritatively about so many subjects a genius, or a dilettante?
能够权威地写出这么多题材的人是个天才还是一个小天才？
In an ambitious biography, Andrew Robinson argues that Young is a good contender to be described as “the last man who knew everything”.
Andrew Robinson在一份雄心勃勃的传记中争辩说，Young是一个好竞争者，可以称为“最后一个知道一切的人”。

Young has competition, however: the phrase, which Robinson uses as the title of his biography of Young, also serves as the subtitle of two other recent biographies – Leonard Warren’s 1998 life of palaeontologist Joseph Leidy (1823–1891) and Paula Findlen’s 2004 book on Athanasius Kircher (1602–1680).
但年轻人有竞争：鲁滨逊用这个词作为他的《年轻的传记》的标题，同时也是最近另外两个传记的副标题 — — Leonard Warren1998年古生物学家Joseph Leid(1823-1891年)和Paula Findlen2004年关于Athanasius Kircher(1602-1680年)的书。

paragraphs.brief: 当然，年轻人所做的不仅仅是写百科全书。
sentences: Young, of course, did more than write encyclopaedia entries.
当然，年轻人所做的不仅仅是写百科全书。
He presented his first paper, on the human eye, to the prestigious academic institution, the Royal Society of London, at the age of 20 and was elected a Fellow of the Society shortly afterwards.
他于20岁时向著名的学术机构伦敦皇家学会提交了第一篇关于人眼的论文，不久后当选为该协会的研究员。
In the paper, which sought to explain how the eye focuses on objects at varying distances, Young hypothesised that this was achieved by changes in the shape of the lens.
在试图解释眼睛如何以不同距离的物体为焦点的文件中，Young假设这是通过镜头形状的变化实现的。

He also theorised that light travels in waves and believed that, to be able to see in colour, there must be three receptors in the eye corresponding to the three principal colours (red, green and violet) to which the retina could respond.
他还认为，光是用波浪飘移，并认为，为了能够以颜色显示，眼睛中必须有三个与视网膜可以响应的三种主要颜色(红色、绿色和紫色)相对应的受体。
All these hypotheses were subsequently proved correct.
所有这些假设后来证明是正确的。

paragraphs.brief: 年轻在40多岁的时候帮助破解了密码解开了1799年拿破仑军队在埃及发现的罗斯塔石上未知的剧本
sentences: Later in his life, when he was in his forties, Young was instrumental in cracking the code that unlocked the unknown script on the Rosetta Stone, a tablet found in Egypt by the Napoleonic army in 1799.
年轻在40多岁的时候帮助破解了密码解开了1799年拿破仑军队在埃及发现的罗斯塔石上未知的剧本
The stone has text in three alphabets: Greek, Egyptian hieroglyphs and another script that was originally unrecognisable.
石头有三种字母的文字：希腊文、埃及象形文字和另一个原本无法辨认的脚本。
The unrecognisable script is now known as demotic and, as Young deduced, is directly related to Egyptian hieroglyphs.
无法辨识的脚本现在被称为 " 低调 "，正如Young推断的，与埃及象形文字直接相关。
His initial work on this appeared in the Britannica entry ‘Egypt’.
他关于此事的初步工作出现在《Egypt》中。
In another entry, Young coined the term ‘Indo-European’ to describe the family of languages spoken throughout most of Europe and northern India.
在另一篇文章中，Young创造了`印欧语 ' 一词，用来描述整个欧洲和印度北部所讲语言的家庭。
These works are landmark achievements for a man who was a child prodigy but who, unlike many remarkable children, did not fade into obscurity as an adult.
对于一个曾是儿童天才、但与许多杰出儿童不同，没有在成人时变成愚昧的人来说，这些作品是具有里程碑意义的成就。

paragraphs.brief: 1773年出生于英格兰萨默塞特，杨从小就与他的祖父一起生活。
sentences: Born in 1773 in Somerset, England, Young lived with his maternal grandfather from an early age.
1773年出生于英格兰萨默塞特，杨从小就与他的祖父一起生活。
He devoured books from the age of two and excelled at Latin, Greek, mathematics and natural philosophy (the 18th-century term for science).
他从两岁开始就吃书并擅长拉丁语、希腊语、数学和自然哲学(18世纪科学学术语)。
After leaving school, he was greatly encouraged by Richard Brocklesby, a physician and Fellow of the Royal Society.
离开学校后，皇家学会的医生兼研究员理查德·布洛克斯比使他深受鼓舞。
Following Brocklesby’s lead, Young decided to pursue a career in medicine.
在布罗克斯比的带领下，杨决定从事医学事业。
He studied in London and then moved on to more formal education in Edinburgh, Göttingen and Cambridge.
他在伦敦学习，然后在爱丁堡、哥廷根和剑桥接受更多的正规教育。
After completing his medical training at the University of Cambridge in 1808, Young set up practice as a physician in London and, a few years later, was appointed physician at St George’s Hospital.
1808年在剑桥大学完成医学培训后，杨在伦敦开业，几年后被任命为圣乔治医院的医生。

paragraphs.brief: 然而，年轻人作为医生的技巧并不等同于他作为自然哲学或语言学学者的才华。
sentences: Young’s skill as a physician, however, did not equal his talent as a scholar of natural philosophy or linguistics.
然而，年轻人作为医生的技巧并不等同于他作为自然哲学或语言学学者的才华。
In 1801, he had been appointed to a professorship of natural philosophy at the Royal Institution, where he delivered as many as 60 lectures a year.
1801年，他被任命为皇家学院自然哲学教授，每年在那里发表多达60次演讲。
His opinions were sought by civic and national authorities on matters such as the introduction of gas lighting to London streets and methods of ship construction.
公民和国家当局就伦敦街道使用燃气灯和船舶建造方法等问题征求了他的意见。
From 1819, he was Superintendent of the Nautical Almanac and Secretary to the Board of Longitude.
1819年，他担任航空神盾局总监和经度委员会秘书。
Between 1816 and 1825, he contributed many entries to the Encyclopaedia Britannica, and throughout his career he authored numerous other essays, papers and books.
1816年至1825年期间，他为百科全书《英国百科全书》投稿，并在职业生涯中撰写了许多其他论文、论文和书籍。

paragraphs.brief: 年轻是传记的完美主题，完美，但令人生畏。
sentences: Young is a perfect subject for a biography – perfect, but daunting.
年轻是传记的完美主题，完美，但令人生畏。
Few men contributed so much to so many technical fields.
很少有男人对如此众多的技术领域作出如此重大的贡献。
Robinson’s aim is to introduce non-scientists to Young’s work and life.
鲁滨逊的目的是让非科学家了解Young的工作和生活。
He succeeds, providing clear expositions of the technical material (especially that on optics and Egyptian hieroglyphs).
他成功地提供了技术材料(尤其是关于光学和埃及象形文字的材料)的清晰说明。
Some readers of this book will, like Robinson, find Young’s accomplishments impressive; others will see him, as some historians have, as a dilettante.
这本书的一些读者会像罗宾逊一样，认为杨的成绩令人印象深刻；其他人会像一些历史学家一样，将他视为一名杰出人士。
Yet despite the rich material presented in this book, readers will not end up knowing Young personally.
然而，尽管这本书提供了丰富的资料，但读者最终不会亲自认识青年。

We catch glimpses of a playful Young, doodling Greek and Latin phrases in his notes on medical lectures and translating the verses that a young lady had written on the walls of a summerhouse into Greek elegiacs.
我们也能一窥杨俏皮的一面：他在医学课笔记里随手写些希腊语和拉丁语，还把一位年轻女子题在凉亭墙上的诗改译成希腊挽歌体。
Young was introduced into elite society, attended the theatre and learned to dance and play the flute.
年轻人被引入精英社会，参加戏剧活动，学会跳舞和吹笛。
In addition, he was an accomplished horseman.
此外，他是一个出色的骑手。
However, his personal life looks pale next to his vibrant career and studies.
但是，他的私人生活看起来与他充满活力的职业生涯和学习相邻。

paragraphs.brief: 1804年，年轻的Eliza Maxwell结了婚，据Robinson说，“他们的婚姻很幸福，她赞赏他的工作”。
sentences: Young married Eliza Maxwell in 1804, and according to Robinson, “their marriage was happy and she appreciated his work”.
1804年，年轻的Eliza Maxwell结了婚，据Robinson说，“他们的婚姻很幸福，她赞赏他的工作”。
Almost all we know about her is that she sustained her husband through some acrimonious disputes about optics and that she worried about money when his medical career was slow to take off.
我们几乎只知道她丈夫经历了一些关于光学的激烈争论而当他医疗生涯缓慢时她担心钱
Little evidence survives concerning the complexities of Young’s relationships with his mother and father, and Robinson does not credit them with shaping Young’s extraordinary mind.
很少有证据能证明杨与其父母关系的复杂性鲁滨逊并不认为他们能塑造杨的非凡头脑
Despite the lack of personal detail, anyone interested in what it means to be a genius should read this book.
尽管缺乏个人细节任何对天才的意义感兴趣的人应该读一读这本书

items.en: Other people have been referred to as ‘the last man who knew everything’.
items.zh: 其他人则被称为「最后一个知道一切的人」。
items.why: 第 2 段提到,“the last man who knew everything”这一说法还被用作 Joseph Leidy 和 Athanasius Kircher 传记的副标题，可见不止 Young 一人曾被如此称呼。

items.en: The fact that Young’s childhood brilliance continued into adulthood was normal.
items.zh: 年轻人的童年才华持续到成年，这是正常的。
items.why: 许多神童成年后变得默默无闻，杨却继续取得重大成就，所以他的经历并不寻常。

items.en: Young’s talents as a doctor are described as surpassing his other skills.
items.zh: 年轻人作为医生的天赋被描述为超越了其他技能。
items.why: 文章明说杨的医术比不上他在自然哲学或语言学上的才能，题干将高低顺序颠倒。

items.en: Young’s advice was sought by several bodies responsible for local and national matters.
items.zh: 负责地方和国家事务的若干机构征求了青年的意见。
items.why: 第 6 段提到，他的意见被“civic and national authorities”征询，既有地方也有国家机构，因此说“多个机构向他请教” 属实。

items.en: All Young’s written works were published in the Encyclopaedia Britannica.
items.zh: 所有Young的著作都刊登在《百科全书》上。
items.why: 第 6 段说明,Young 除了给 Encyclopaedia Britannica 投稿，还撰写了“numerous other essays, papers and books”,并非所有著作都发表在百科全书中。

items.en: Young was interested in a range of social pastimes.
items.zh: 年轻人对各种社会消遣感兴趣
items.why: 杨进入社交圈，去剧院、学跳舞和吹长笛，说明他有多种社交消遣。

items.en: Young suffered from poor health in his later years.
items.zh: 年轻人在以后的几年里身体状况很差。
items.why: 文章交代杨行医并获医院任命的经历，没有证据说明他本人晚年健康不佳。

items.en: How many life stories did Thomas Young write for the Encyclopaedia Britannica?
items.zh: 托马斯·杨为百科全书写了多少人生故事？
items.why: 第 2 段: 他为 Brtannica 撰写了“46 biographical entries”。

items.en: What was the subject of Thomas Young’s first academic paper?
items.zh: 托马斯·杨的第一份学术论文的主题是什么？
items.why: 第 3 段开头:“他在 20 岁时提交的首篇论文关于人眼"。

items.en: What name did Young give to a group of languages?
items.zh: 杨给一组语言取了什么名字？
items.why: 第 4段:“Young 创造了 Indo-European 一词”。

items.en: Who inspired Young to enter the medical profession?
items.zh: 是谁激励杨进医学界的？
items.why: 第 5 段:“他受到医生、皇家学会会员 Richard Brocklesby 的极大鼓励”。

items.en: At which place of higher learning did Young hold a teaching position?
items.zh: 在哪个高等教育机构担任教师职位？
items.why: 第 6 段:“1801年，他被任命为 Royal Institution 自然哲学教授”。

items.en: What was the improvement to London roads on which Young’s ideas were sought?
items.zh: 伦敦公路在寻求Young的想法方面有什么改进？
items.why: 第 6 段:“他的意见被征询，用于在伦敦街道引入煤气照明 (gas lighting)”.

groups.label: 简答题
groups.instructionsZh: 根据原文简答。每题最多填三个词，可含数字。

pairs: 题干所说的人生故事在百科全书中就是传记条目。
原文把一组有亲缘关系的语言称为一个语族。
第 6 段 · 第 9 句
第 2 段 · 第 1 句
points: 文章交代杨行医并获医院任命的经历，没有证据说明他本人晚年健康不佳。
第 4段:“Young 创造了 Indo-European 一词”。
clauses: In an ambitious biography, Andrew Robinson argues … ”.
“that Young is a good contender to be described as “the last man who knew everything”补足 argues 的内容，交代究竟在说、判断或发现什么。
先读 argues 所在的主句，再把 that 后面的内容作为一个整体。

Young has competition, however: the phrase, …, also serves as the subtitle of two other recent biographies – Leonard Warren’s 1998 life of palaeontologist Joseph Leidy (1823–1891) and Paula Findlen’s 2004 book on Athanasius Kircher (1602–1680).
“which Robinson uses as the title of his biography of Young”修饰前面的 phrase。先认出先行词，再读从句补充的特征。
读到 which 时，回看 phrase，再把修饰信息接回主句。
lead: In the 21st century, it would be quite impossible for even the most learned man to know everything.
在21世纪，即使是最有学识的人也不可能知道一切
However, as recently as the 18th century, there were those whose knowledge encompassed most of the information available at that time.
然而，直到18世纪，还有一些人的知识涵盖了当时所掌握的大部分信息。
This is a review of a biography of one such man.
这是对一个这样的人的传记的回顾
